Category probabilities of an ordinal fit

Source: R/ordinal_methods.R
ordinal_probabilities.Rd

fitted() returns, for each row the model was fitted to, the posterior mean probability of each category, at the fitted values of the random effects. predict() returns the same probabilities for the rows of newdata, with the random effects set to zero, or with marginal = TRUE integrated over their fitted variances, which is the probability for a new unit in a new block.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'flexybayes_ordinal'
fitted(object, n_draws = 1000L, seed = NULL, summary = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexybayes_ordinal'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  marginal = FALSE,
  n_draws = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An ordinal fit, from flexybayes() with family = "cumulative" or "cratio".

n_draws

The number of posterior draws. Default 1000. On brms it is at most the number the sampler stored.

seed

An integer seed for the draws, or NULL (the default) to use the session's random number stream.

summary

TRUE (the default) returns the posterior mean. FALSE returns every draw.

...

Ignored by fitted(). In predict(), an argument of the other predict() methods that has no meaning here is refused by name.

newdata

A data frame holding the fixed-effect variables, or NULL (the default) for the rows the model was fitted to.

marginal

FALSE (the default) sets every random effect to zero. TRUE integrates over them.

Value

A matrix with one row per row of the data and one column per category, named by the category labels. With summary = FALSE, an array, draws by rows by categories.

Details

Each probability is averaged over n_draws joint posterior draws of the thresholds, the coefficients and the variances, so it carries the uncertainty of all three. With marginal = TRUE the random terms of a new unit enter as one normal deviation whose variance is the sum of the fitted variances (random intercepts, their interactions and an AR1 field, whose marginal variance is its fitted variance), and the probability is integrated over it by 40-node Gauss-Hermite quadrature in each draw. On brms, fitted() reads brms::posterior_epred().

The probability of a set of categories is the sum of their columns, for example rowSums(p[, c("Z5", "Z6")]) for a stage of Z5 or later.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  d <- data.frame(
    trt = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), each = 60)),
    block = factor(rep(1:6, times = 20))
  )
  eta <- 0.8 * (d$trt == "b") + rnorm(6, 0, 0.3)[d$block]
  d$score <- cut(eta + rlogis(120), c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, Inf),
    labels = c("low", "mid", "high", "top"), ordered_result = TRUE)
  fit <- flexybayes(score ~ trt, random = ~block, data = d,
    family = "cumulative", backend = "inla", verbose = FALSE)
  head(fitted(fit, seed = 1L))
  predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(trt = c("a", "b")), marginal = TRUE,
    seed = 1L)
}
